about: Steven K. Deutsch is an experienced attorney and a partner at Deutsch & Blumberg, P.A., in Miami, Florida. Mr. Deutsch focuses his practice on general personal injury, representing clients who have been injured in accidents such as motor vehicle accidents. He also works with cases involving medical and dental malpractice, product liability and insurance coverage disputes.

A graduate of New York University, Mr. Deutsch obtained his law degree from the University of Miami School of Law. He is also certified in civil trial law by The Florida Bar and the National Board of Trial Advocacy.

Admitted to practice in the state of Florida in 1974, Mr. Deutsch is also admitted to appear before the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of Florida, the U.S. Courts of Appeals for the Eleventh Circuit and the Supreme Court of the United States.

In his more than four decades of legal practice, Mr. Deutsch has earned a number of honors and awards in recognition of his hard work and professionalism. He is rated AV Preeminent,* the highest possible rating, by the notable peer review service Martindale-Hubbell. He has also been featured in the publication "The Best Lawyers in America."

Active in professional organizations, Mr. Deutsch is a member of the National Board of Trial Advocacy. He has also served in various roles in different groups over the course of his years in practice, including The Florida Bar Rules of Evidence Committee and Civil Procedure Committee. He also participates in a wide variety of community activities and events.

*AV®, AV Preeminent®, Martindale-Hubbell Distinguished and Martindale-Hubbell Notable are certification marks used under license in accordance with the Martindale-Hubbell certification procedures, standards and policies. Martindale-Hubbell® is the facilitator of a peer review rating process. Ratings reflect the anonymous opinions of members of the bar and the judiciary. Martindale-Hubbell® Peer Review Rating™ fall into two categories – legal ability and general ethical standards.
